title: Duke Energy Foundation awards $100,000 in grants to help families in need of critical home repairs
summary: The Duke Energy Foundation recently awarded $100,000 in grants to four regional nonprofit organizations to help seniors and low-income homeowners make critical home repairs that will keep them safe and warm this winter season while also helping them manage their energy costs.
body_markdown:
-


### **Grants were distributed to four local nonprofits in Greater Cincinnati, Clermont County, Ohio, and Northern Kentucky**


-


### **Funding helps residents stay safe and warm in their homes while managing their energy costs**


CINCINNATI – The Duke Energy Foundation recently awarded $100,000 in grants to four regional nonprofit organizations to help seniors and low-income homeowners make critical home repairs that will keep them safe and warm this winter season while also helping them manage their energy costs.


Grant funding will support emergency and health and safety repairs, furnace repairs and replacements, weatherization and energy efficiency improvements, and accessibility modifications.


“As cold temperatures and the holiday season approach, a broken furnace, leaking roof or missing ramp can quickly become a crisis for seniors and families on a tight budget,” said Amy Spiller, president of Duke Energy Ohio & Kentucky. “These partners have deep roots in our communities, and we’re proud to support their work in helping our neighbors stay safe and warm in the homes they love.”


**How will the grants help local residents?**


For many older adults and low-income homeowners, essential repairs may be out of reach. A repaired furnace, new roof or an accessibility ramp can make their homes safer, more comfortable and more affordable. These repairs reduce energy burden and give families greater stability.


**What they are saying**


**Billie Kuntz, Executive Director,** **Clermont County Community Services Inc.:** “This grant from the Duke Energy Foundation will help Clermont County families make essential repairs so they can stay safe and comfortable in their homes. We’re grateful for the Foundation’s support and what it will mean for the families we serve.”


**Rhonda Chisenhall, Chief Advancement Officer, Northern Kentucky Community Action Commission:** “We are incredibly grateful to the Duke Energy Foundation for its generous investment in the families and communities we serve. For many low-income homeowners, the cost of critical home repairs is a barrier to making their homes safe. This funding will help remove those barriers, allowing us to make homes safer, more energy efficient and more affordable to maintain. Duke Energy Foundation's partnership is about more than repairing homes – it’s about providing stability, reducing financial burdens, and improving the quality of life for families across Northern Kentucky. Together, we are creating a lasting impact, one home and one family at a time.”


**Brandon Holmes, Executive Director of Community Development, City of Covington, Ky:** "By providing assistance with critical home improvements, the Homeowner Assistance Program helps preserve our housing stock, strengthen our neighborhoods, and ensure that longtime residents can continue to live safely and comfortably in their homes. We are incredibly grateful to Duke Energy for its generous contribution to the Fund for Covington and its continued commitment to investing in our community. This partnership will help us make a meaningful difference in the lives of some Covington homeowners facing financial barriers."


**Duke Energy Foundation**


The Duke Energy Foundation provides nearly $30 million annually in philanthropic support to meet the needs of communities where Duke Energy customers live and work. The Foundation is funded by Duke Energy shareholders.


**Duke Energy**


Duke Energy (NYSE: DUK), a Fortune 150 company headquartered in Charlotte, N.C., is one of America’s largest energy holding companies. The company’s electric utilities serve 8.7 million customers in North Carolina, South Carolina, Florida, Indiana, Ohio and Kentucky, and collectively own 55,700 megawatts of energy capacity. Its natural gas utilities serve 1.6 million customers in North Carolina, South Carolina, Ohio and Kentucky.


Duke Energy is executing an energy modernization strategy, keeping customer value at the forefront as it invests in electric grid upgrades and efficient generation resources to strengthen the system and serve growing energy needs.
